prop:ns-kummer-specialisation:
Proposition Kummer specialisation: the NS obstruction survives q = 1 for \gcd(\chi(A), n) \neq n. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) isolate a valid QOU whose Reeb bundle \xi over the closed surface \mathcal{S} has class [\xi] \in H^1(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) and first obstruction \kappa_0 = c_1(\xi) = e(\xi) \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{Z}), and suppose \xi is the unit tangent bundle of \mathcal{S}. Then \kappa_0[\mathcal{S}] = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}) by Poincaré--Hopf (QU-to-QOU, item 2). The hypothesis is not supplied by the Reeb bundle \mathcal{R}_p, which is the Hopf fibration over the fibre \mathcal{S}_p \cong S^2 with Euler number -1. For the Descartes universe it holds for the link of the canonical cone over Bring's curve, UT(\Sigma_4), with Euler number -6 (the cone link). The integer that controls the Kummer tower is therefore \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}), a topological Euler characteristic, and not the categorical trace \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) (the three Euler characteristics).

The strict Kummer exact sequence evaluated at any integer n \geq 1:

  1 \to \mu_n \to \mathbb{G}_m
  \xrightarrow{(\cdot)^n} \mathbb{G}_m \to 1

forces a long exact sequence mapping through cohomology:

  H^1(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m)
  \xrightarrow{\cdot n}
  H^1(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m)
  \xrightarrow{\partial_n}
  H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n)
  \to H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) = 0.

On a closed surface H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) = 0, so \partial_n is surjective; its source modulo n is \mathbb{Z}/n via the degree (the degree-zero part of H^1(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) is divisible), and H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n) \cong \mathbb{Z}/n. The specialisation driving q = 1 projects cleanly:

  \kappa_0 \mapsto
  \partial_n[\xi] = \kappa_0 \bmod n
   \in 
  H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n) \cong \mathbb{Z}/n,

which is the obstruction to an n-th root of \xi (QU-to-QOU, item 3).

The resulting class avoids zero if and only if n \nmid \kappa_0, that is, if and only if \xi has no n-th root. Evaluated against any QOU with \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}) \neq 0:

  1. The exact specialisation \kappa_0|_{q=1} avoids zero within H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n) for all integers n \nmid \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}).
  2. The integer set \{n : n \nmid \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S})\} extends to infinity (encompassing all primes not dividing \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S})), so the obstruction remains persistently nonzero, piercing infinitely many levels of the Kummer tower.
  3. The obstruction vanishes only at the finite, isolated Kummer levels n \mid \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}), which align with the finite set of roots of unity where the category's truncation is compatible with the fixed Euler class.

What persistence does and does not buy (the genericity caveat). Items 2 and 3 say the set of surviving Kummer levels is cofinite. That measures how cheap the condition is, not how strong — and here the cofiniteness is elementary arithmetic: only n \in \{1, 2, 3, 6\} divide -6, so the obstruction persists at every other level for no reason having to do with fluid dynamics. (The analogous statement for the aether parameter q — a nonzero polynomial obstruction has cofinite non-vanishing locus — is a parallel fact over a different index set, not the same one, and does not support the level-indexed claim.) A cheap condition cannot by itself be equivalent to a uniform statement without collapsing the equivalence.

Consequently "persistently nonzero" is not by itself evidence that the NS obstruction is a faithful regularity criterion.

Note also that the divisibility structure is what makes the verdict level-dependent: at \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}) = -6 the obstruction vanishes at levels n \in \{1, 2, 3, 6\} while persisting at all others. Different root-of-unity specialisations of \kappa_0 therefore carry different Kummer verdicts at once, and non-vanishing of \kappa_0 \bmod n at generic n transfers no analytical blowup conclusion to the hydrodynamic limit.

The regularity content therefore sits in the filtration — whether the vortex-knot complexity stays bounded — not in the non-vanishing of the class alone.

Proof.

(a) Divisibility of the Euler class.

Constrained over a closed orientable surface \Sigma_g anchored at genus g: H^2(\Sigma_g, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}. Under the hypothesis on \xi, the Euler class evaluates to e(\xi)[\Sigma_g] = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\Sigma_g) = 2 - 2g \in \mathbb{Z}. Therefore:

  \kappa_0 \bmod n = 0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  n \mid \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}).

Applied to the Descartes universe at \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}) = -6, the valid divisors restrict strictly to \{1, 2, 3, 6\}. \kappa_0 \bmod n mathematically zeroes out only spanning n \in \{1, 2, 3, 6\}. It rigorously evades zero for all other n (verifiably holding for n = 5, 7, 11, 13, \ldots).

(b) Obstruction persistence.

Evaluating at the root of unity q = e^{i\pi/\kappa}, the operating Kummer level isolates strictly to n = 2\kappa (reflecting the exact order mapping q inside \mathbb{G}_m). The functional obstruction \kappa_0 \bmod 2\kappa reduces to:

  \kappa_0 \bmod 2\kappa = 0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  2\kappa \mid \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}).

For \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}) = -6, 2\kappa \mid 6 permits exclusively \kappa \in \{1, 3\}, corresponding to q = e^{i\pi} or q = e^{i\pi/3}. At every other valid \kappa (universally capturing all \kappa \geq 4), the obstruction fundamentally persists squarely at that root of unity.

Scope of (b). The identification of the order of the root of unity q with the Kummer level n of the Reeb bundle is asserted, not derived; the arithmetic 2\kappa \nmid 6 for \kappa \notin \{1, 3\} holds independently of it. The class \kappa_0 \bmod n is a global class on \mathcal{S}: its restriction to a one-dimensional locus lies in H^2(\Sigma, \mu_n) = 0.

(c) The limit as kappa goes to infinity.

Pushing \kappa \to \infty (q \to 1) forces 2\kappa \to \infty. Consequently, 2\kappa \nmid 6 governs unconditionally for all \kappa \geq 4. The math yields:

  \kappa_0 \bmod 2\kappa  \neq  0
  \qquad\text{for all } \kappa \geq 4.

The topological component driving the NS obstruction rigorously avoids vanishing through the q \to 1 classical limit. Items 1–3 follow: the vanishing set is exactly \{n : n \mid \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S})\}, finite and complementary to the infinitely many levels where \kappa_0 \bmod n \neq 0.
rem:ns-kummer-specialisation-consequence:
Remark Consequence for internal NS-singularity and its curve-restriction limit. For a QOU over a closed surface \mathcal{S} with \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}) = -6, the Kummer specialisation gives a non-zero global class \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}) \bmod n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n) at every level n \notin \{1, 2, 3, 6\}. In the internal surface classification, this places the model in the categorically NS-singular class (\mathrm{NS}(A) = e(\xi) = -6 \neq 0).

This global Kummer non-divisibility does not, however, produce a non-zero curve restriction \kappa_n|_\Sigma or establish finite-time blowup for the classical Navier--Stokes equation. Item 3 of QU-to-QOU holds in the Kummer cohomology groups H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n) rather than as a complementary-subgroup splitting inside H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m), which vanishes on a closed surface (H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) = 0). Furthermore, on any one-dimensional collision locus \Sigma \subset \mathcal{S}, the restriction e(\xi)|_\Sigma vanishes identically because H^2(\Sigma, \cdot) = 0. The non-zero class \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}) \bmod n therefore obstructs n-th roots of the Reeb bundle on \mathcal{S} for n \nmid 6, without deciding regularity of the three-dimensional PDE.
thm:ns-singularity-descartes:
Theorem Topology of the Reeb bundle of the Descartes universe. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be the Descartes quantum universe, with base Bring's surface \mathcal{S} of genus 4 and \chi(\mathcal{S}) = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6. Let \xi be its Reeb \mathrm{U}(1)-bundle, the unit tangent bundle of \mathcal{S}. Then:

  1. e(\xi) = c_1(\xi) = -6 \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}. In particular \xi has no nowhere-vanishing section.
  2. For n \geq 1, \xi has an n-th root if and only if n \in \{1, 2, 3, 6\}. For every other n the obstruction -6 \bmod n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n) \cong \mathbb{Z}/n is non-zero.
  3. For any one-dimensional locus \Sigma \subset \mathcal{S}, the restriction of each of these classes to \Sigma is zero, since H^2(\Sigma, \cdot) = 0.
prf:ns-singularity-descartes:
Proof Proof of ns singularity descartes. Item 1: by QU-to-QOU, item 2, e(\xi) = c_1(\xi) = \chi(\mathcal{S}) = -6 for the unit tangent bundle. A nowhere-vanishing section would trivialise \xi and force e(\xi) = 0.

Item 2: by QU-to-QOU, item 3, \xi has an n-th root if and only if n \mid \chi(\mathcal{S}) = -6, with obstruction -6 \bmod n; see also the Kummer specialisation. The positive divisors of 6 are 1, 2, 3, 6.

Item 3: \Sigma has dimension 1, so H^2(\Sigma, M) = 0 for every coefficient group M (Godement II.5.12).

Scope of the curve restriction. Item 2 holds for the global class on \mathcal{S} (\kappa_0 \bmod 2\kappa for \kappa \geq 4), whereas on \mathcal{S} the jet corrections \delta_n lie in the image of H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{S}}) = 0 and on any one-dimensional locus \Sigma \subset \mathcal{S} the restriction e(\xi)|_\Sigma vanishes identically by item 3. Moreover, the core-Levi form yields a single Levi scalar \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi, and an explicit Beltrami solution refutes the implication from non-degenerate Levi data to finite-time blow-up (branch (A) of the Levi degeneracy conjecture). Conditional blow-up criteria via vorticity lower bounds and BKM divergence require a non-vanishing cohomological obstruction on \Sigma, which does not exist when \dim \Sigma = 1. Whether the Reeb field vanishes dynamically along \Sigma is a separate PDE question outside the scope of this theorem. \square
rem:ns-singularity-descartes-interpretat: Remark What \chi(\mathcal{S})=-6 fixes about the Reeb bundle, and what it does not. What the theorem says. The Euler characteristic \chi(\mathcal{S}) = -6 of Bring's surface fixes the topology of the Reeb bundle \xi: its Euler class is -6, so \xi has no nowhere-vanishing section, and \xi has an n-th root exactly for n \in \{1, 2, 3, 6\}. These are statements about the global class on the surface \mathcal{S}. On any one-dimensional locus \Sigma every such class restricts to zero, so the theorem gives no obstruction on a vortex-collision curve and no statement about blow-up of a flow.
ex:torus-ns-regular:
Example The torus quantum universe: \chi(A) = 0 and NS regularity. Assume (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) represents a valid quantum universe placing A on the classical 2-torus \Sigma_1 (genus g = 1). Its Euler characteristic is

  \chi(A) = 2 - 2g = 0.

The global NS obstruction vanishes. Under the global surface definition (NS-regular QOU), the NS obstruction is the global Euler class of the Reeb bundle \xi on \mathcal{S} = \Sigma_1, whose degree is \deg e(\xi) = \mathrm{tr}(\kappa_0) = \chi(A) = 0. Hence the global class vanishes directly in H^2(\Sigma_1, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}:

  \mathrm{NS}(A) = e(\xi) = 0 \in H^2(\Sigma_1, \mathbb{Z}),

and for every integer n \geq 1 its Kummer reduction \chi(A) \bmod n \in H^2(\Sigma_1, \mu_n) vanishes identically (Kummer specialisation). Restricting \kappa_0 to a one-dimensional collision locus \Sigma would give 0 vacuously on every curve because H^2(\Sigma, \cdot) = 0; defined on the global surface \mathcal{S}, \mathrm{NS}(A) = 0 on \Sigma_1 contrasts non-degenerately with \mathrm{NS}(A) = -6 \neq 0 on Bring's surface \Sigma_4.

The torus quantum universe is therefore categorically NS-regular.

Physical meaning and 2D vs 3D Navier--Stokes scope. Because e(\xi) = 0, the unit tangent bundle of \Sigma_1 is trivial and admits a nowhere-vanishing section. For a 2D incompressible fluid directly on the surface \Sigma_1 = \mathbb{T}^2, global regularity for all smooth initial data is a classical PDE theorem (Ladyzhenskaya), owing to 2D vorticity conservation rather than to a vanishing cohomology class. By contrast, the categorical label \mathrm{NS}(A) = 0 does not establish global regularity for classical unforced 3D Navier--Stokes (such as Fefferman's Alternative B on \mathbb{T}^3): by Tao's averaged Navier--Stokes barrier (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 29 (2016), 601--674), no argument that depends only on topology and ignores the structure of the 3D advection nonlinearity B(u, u) = P[(u \cdot \nabla)u] can prove 3D global regularity, and the q \to 1 limit at \nu_q = (q - 1)/(2q) is the inviscid Euler limit unless taken along the fixed-\hbar_q scaling branch. Nor does torus regularity arise from core flattening via Levi-eigenvalue degeneration: on the three-dimensional flow domain the Levi datum of the vorticity plane field reduces to a single scalar rather than an eigenvalue pair (core Levi form).

Failure of the torus to support the observed physics. Because the torus anchors at g = 1, it physically embeds exactly one torus knot: T_{2,3} (the generic trefoil spanning Seifert genus 1). The generated knot spectrum isolates a single physical generator — effectively abandoning the muon, the tau, and any quarks outside the first generation. The explicit representation theory governing \pi_1(\Sigma_1) = \mathbb{Z}^2 behaves completely abelian: every valid \mathrm{SU}(2) representation must mechanically factor down through \mathrm{U}(1). The base gauge group completely collapses. The expected full particle spectrum simply cannot emerge.

The torus also fails observability. Evaluated over \Sigma_1, explicitly flat \mathrm{SU}(2) connections reliably exist bearing holonomy restricted to \mathrm{U}(1) \subset \mathrm{SU}(2). These remaining connections act entirely reducible: H^0(\Sigma_1, \mathrm{Ad}(P)) \neq 0 (the isolated Cartan subalgebra \mathfrak{u}(1) \subset \mathfrak{su}(2) automatically supplies a persistent nonzero equivariant section). Consequently, \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) \neq 0. The core observability axiom explicitly fails.

The resulting torus structure forms a quantum pre-universe (QPU), definitively rejecting QOU status.

Contrast with the Descartes universe.

See Table.

The mathematical torus provides the simplest mechanical example where \chi(\mathcal{S}) = 0 yields categorical NS-regularity (\mathrm{NS}(A) = e(\xi) = 0). Predictably, it is also physically trivial: the vanishing Euler characteristic prevents the torus from supporting an irreducible QOU.

Other \chi = 0 examples (2D spectral surfaces vs 3-manifolds). Any genus-1 spectral surface \mathcal{S} has \chi(\mathcal{S}) = 0 (such as the flat 2-torus \mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}^2 or a complex elliptic curve) and is categorically NS-regular in the same sense. Scope note on 3-manifolds: closed orientable 3-manifolds M^3 — such as \mathbb{T}^3, the Heisenberg nilmanifold \mathrm{Heis}(\mathbb{Z}) \backslash \mathrm{Heis}(\mathbb{R}), Seifert 3-manifolds, and the unit tangent bundle \mathrm{UT}(\Sigma_4) of Bring's surface — satisfy \chi(M^3) = 0 automatically by Poincaré duality, whereas \mathrm{NS}(A) = e(\xi) \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{Z}) is defined on the 2D spectral surface \mathcal{S} and does not settle 3D Navier--Stokes regularity on M^3.

prop:reeb-beltrami-regular-flow:
Proposition The fibre-rotation field of \mathrm{UT}(\Sigma_4) is a regular Navier--Stokes flow. Let \Sigma_4 = \Gamma\backslash\mathbb{H} be Bring's surface with its hyperbolic metric of curvature -1, where \Gamma \subset \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}) is a torsion-free Fuchsian group of genus 4. Let M = \mathrm{UT}(\Sigma_4) \cong \Gamma\backslash\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}) be its unit tangent bundle, the total space of the Reeb bundle of the Descartes universe. In \mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{R}) put

  X = \tfrac{1}{2}H, \qquad Y = \tfrac{1}{2}(E + F), \qquad V = \tfrac{1}{2}(E - F),

so that [X, Y] = V, [X, V] = Y and [Y, V] = -X. The left-invariant extensions of X, Y, V descend to M, and V generates the rotation of the circle fibres of M \to \Sigma_4. For s > 0 let g_s be the left-invariant metric whose matrix in the frame (X, Y, V) is \mathrm{diag}(1, 1, s^2). Orient M by (X, Y, V) and define \mathrm{curl}\,u by (\mathrm{curl}\,u)^\flat = \star\,d u^\flat. Then:

  1. V is a Killing field of g_s, with \mathrm{div}\,V = 0, \nabla_V V = 0 and \mathrm{curl}\,V = -s\,V. The unit field V/s satisfies the same Beltrami equation \mathrm{curl}(V/s) = -s\,(V/s).

  2. \mathrm{curl}\,\mathrm{curl}\,V = s^2 V, \mathrm{Ric}(V) = \tfrac{s^2}{2} V and \nabla^*\nabla V = \tfrac{s^2}{2} V.

  3. Consider the unforced incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on (M, g_s),

      \partial_t u + \nabla_u u + \mathrm{grad}\,p = \nu\,L u, \qquad \mathrm{div}\,u = 0, \qquad \nu \geq 0,

    with one of three viscous operators: the deformation operator L_{\mathrm{Def}} = -(\Delta_H - 2\,\mathrm{Ric}), which equals 2\,\mathrm{div}\,\mathrm{Def} on divergence-free fields [ebin-marsden1970]; the Hodge operator L_H = -\Delta_H; or the Bochner operator L_B = -\nabla^*\nabla. Here \Delta_H is the Hodge Laplacian transported to vector fields by g_s, which equals \mathrm{curl}\,\mathrm{curl} on divergence-free fields. For every a \in \mathbb{R} and every \nu \geq 0, with constant pressure p, the field

      u(t) = a\,V \;\;(L = L_{\mathrm{Def}}), \qquad
  u(t) = a\,e^{-\nu s^2 t}\,V \;\;(L = L_H), \qquad
  u(t) = a\,e^{-\nu s^2 t/2}\,V \;\;(L = L_B)

    is a smooth solution on M \times [0, \infty). Under L_{\mathrm{Def}} it is steady and extends to M \times \mathbb{R}. At \nu = 0 all three reduce to the steady Euler solution u \equiv a\,V.
prf:reeb-beltrami-regular-flow:
Proof Proof of the regular fibre-rotation flow on \mathrm{UT}(\Sigma_4). The group \Gamma acts on \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}) on the left, so left-invariant vector fields, forms and metrics on \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}) descend to M. The Levi-Civita connection of a left-invariant metric maps pairs of left-invariant fields to left-invariant fields, so every quantity in items 1 and 2 is computed on the Lie algebra. The field V generates the fibre rotation because \exp( heta V) rotates unit tangent vectors by the angle heta.

Items 1 and 2 are computations in the basis (X, Y, V). The Koszul formula determines abla on left-invariant fields. The operator \mathrm{ad}_V is skew for g_s, so V is Killing and \mathrm{div}\,V = 0. The remaining values follow from the Koszul connection, from the curvature R(u,v)w = abla_u abla_v w - abla_v abla_u w - abla_{[u,v]} w traced over the orthonormal frame (X, Y, V/s), and from the definition of \mathrm{curl}. The values satisfy the Weitzenböck identity abla^* abla V + \mathrm{Ric}(V) = \Delta_H V and agree with Milnor's Ricci formula \mathrm{Ric}(X) = -(1 + s^2/2)\,X.

For item 3 write u(t) = a(t)\,V. Then \mathrm{div}\,u = 0 and abla_u u = a^2\, abla_V V = 0 by item 1, so with constant p the equations reduce to a'(t)\,V = u\,a(t)\,L V. By items 1 and 2, L_{\mathrm{Def}} V = -(s^2 - s^2)\,V = 0, L_H V = -s^2 V and L_B V = - frac{s^2}{2} V. This gives a' = 0, a' = - u s^2 a and a' = - frac{ u s^2}{2} a respectively, with the stated solutions. Each u(t) is a smooth multiple of the smooth field V for all t. \square

Exact verification. The Lie-algebra computations above are checked exactly: the brackets, as 2 imes 2 matrix commutators; the identification of the Koszul connection used with the Levi-Civita connection on left-invariant fields; the Killing property of V, which fails for X; the formulas for abla_V V, \mathrm{curl}\,V, \mathrm{curl}\,\mathrm{curl}\,V, \mathrm{Ric}\,V, \mathrm{Ric}\,X, abla^* abla V and the Weitzenböck identity for V; and the identity (\Delta_H - 2\,\mathrm{Ric})\,V = 0.

The flat analogue is also proved end to end: a Beltrami eigenfield yields an exact Navier--Stokes solution, and the ABC field gives the solution e^{- u t} u_{\mathrm{ABC}} on the three-torus.

Two standard steps are not verified here and are taken from the standard theory: the descent of left-invariant data from \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}) to \Gamma ackslash\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}), and the identification of the manifold operators abla, \mathrm{Ric}, abla^* abla and \Delta_H on left-invariant fields with the Lie-algebra formulas above. The reduction of the equations to the scalar equation for a(t) in item 3 is carried out by hand.
rem:reeb-beltrami-regular-flow-scope:
Remark Scope of the regular fibre-rotation flow. The proposition exhibits one explicit family of solutions, the multiples of a single field, on one Riemannian 3-manifold. It says nothing about solutions with other initial data. Global regularity on M remains as open as on the three-torus T^3 = \mathrm{UT}(T^2) of the torus example. The proposition does settle a question of topology. The bundle M \to \Sigma_4 has Euler number -6, and this topology carries a smooth global solution. Hence no invariant of the bundle can force every solution on M to blow up, and the explicit family is the witness.

The field V generates the free \mathrm{U}(1) action on the fibres, which is how the Reeb bundle specifies its Reeb field. A finer identification is inherited and is not re-derived here: that V, with this normalisation, is the Reeb field of the Boothby--Wang contact form that M carries as the link of Bring's cone.

The metric parameter s > 0 is a free choice. Up to an overall scale, every left-invariant metric invariant under the fibre rotation has the form g_s, and s = 1 is the Sasaki metric of the hyperbolic surface. The corpus does not fix s. No value of s is compared with data, so the parameter is unconstrained and no fit is involved. The contact form \theta^V dual to V and its Reeb field are independent of s.

The solution the field gives depends on the viscous operator. The three operators agree on flat space, where \mathrm{Ric} = 0, and differ on M. Under the deformation operator the field V is an infinitesimal isometry, so \mathrm{Def}\,V = 0 and the dissipation 2\nu\int_M |\mathrm{Def}\,u|^2 vanishes. This is the curved analogue of solid-body rotation. The kinetic energy \tfrac{1}{2}\int_M |aV|^2 = \tfrac{1}{2}a^2 s^2\,\mathrm{vol}(M) and the helicity \int_M \langle aV, \mathrm{curl}(aV)\rangle = -a^2 s^3\,\mathrm{vol}(M) are conserved.
def:observable-mtc:
Definition Observable modular tensor category at q = \zeta_N. Fix an integer N \geq 3 and set q = \zeta_N = e^{2\pi i / N}, a primitive N-th root of unity. Let \mathbf{C}_{\mathrm{any}}(N) be the truncated category, the quotient of \mathrm{Rep}(U_q(\mathfrak{su}_2)) by the ideal of negligible morphisms [moore-seiberg1989].

The observable modular tensor category at level N is the ribbon fusion category \mathbf{C}_{\mathrm{any}}(N), equipped with the braiding c and ribbon twist \varTheta inherited from the quasi-triangular structure of U_q(\mathfrak{su}_2) at q = \zeta_N.
rem:observable-mtc-remark: Remark Semisimplicity, simple objects and modularity at q = \zeta_N. At q = \zeta_N the representation category \mathrm{Rep}(U_q(\mathfrak{su}_2)) is no longer semisimple; quotienting out the ideal of negligible morphisms yields the truncated category \mathbf{C}_{\mathrm{any}}(N), with finitely many simple objects \mathbf{V}_0, \mathbf{V}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{V}_{N-2} [moore-seiberg1989]. The observable modular tensor category is modular: the S-matrix S_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}(c_{\mathbf{V}_i, \mathbf{V}_j} \circ c_{\mathbf{V}_j, \mathbf{V}_i}) is non-degenerate.
rem:observable-mtc-braiding:
Remark Braiding non-symmetry and the commutative limit of the observable MTC. Braiding non-symmetry. Evaluating N \geq 3 mapping any definitively non-trivial simple object \mathbf{V} \in \mathbf{C}_{\mathrm{any}}(N), the math guarantees

  c_{\mathbf{V}, \mathbf{V}} \circ c_{\mathbf{V}, \mathbf{V}}
    \neq  \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{V} \otimes \mathbf{V}}.

The mathematical braiding strictly refuses to square cleanly back into the identity across valid simples. This functions as the absolute hallmark denoting a genuinely modular (strictly non-symmetric) tensor category. It acts as the rigid absolute prerequisite unlocking valid anyonic statistics.

Relation to the commutative limit. The exact commutative limit executing q \to 1 detailed in Chapter 3 maps directly onto scaling N \to \infty. At this limit, the strict mathematical truncation fully opens up. All negligible morphisms cleanly vanish. The isolated braiding forcibly degenerates backward into a strictly symmetric mathematical structure. Consequently, the two specified specialisations fundamentally separate:

Specialisation q Braiding Anyons
Commutative limit q = 1 strictly symmetric no
Root-of-unity \mathrm{MTC} q = \zeta_N (N \geq 3) strictly non-symmetric yes

The resulting geometric shadow projected exactly upon the genus-2 curve \mathcal{X}_5 detailed in def:hyperelliptic-quintic safely isolates either distinct regime, relying entirely on its fifth-roots-of-unity active branch set. Tracking within the commutative limit, the precise values \zeta_5^{k} rigidly mark pure classical phase defects mounted exactly across a single isolated \mathrm{U}(1) tube. Conversely, evaluating directly at q = \zeta_5, that identical set of discrete data seamlessly labels the valid anyonic fusion channels populating \mathbf{C}_{\mathrm{any}}(5).
prop:bn-mtc-action:
Proposition Braid group action on \mathbf{V}^{\otimes n} does not factor through S_n. Let \mathbf{C}_{\mathrm{any}}(N) define the exact observable modular tensor category detailed in def:observable-mtc, functioning specifically at level N \geq 3. Let \mathbf{V} specify any definitively non-trivial simple object. Evaluating across every n \geq 2, the embedded categorical braiding directly generates a functional representation

  \rho_n \colon B_n  \longrightarrow
   \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbf{C}_{\mathrm{any}}(N)}(\mathbf{V}^{\otimes n}),
  \qquad
  \sigma_i  \longmapsto
   \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{V}^{\otimes (i-1)}}
   \otimes\, c_{\mathbf{V}, \mathbf{V}}
   \otimes\, \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{V}^{\otimes (n - i - 1)}},

governing the Artin braid group B_n (see def:braid-group) mapped onto the tensor power of \mathbf{V}. This representation does not factor through the symmetric-group quotient B_n \twoheadrightarrow S_n.
prf:bn-mtc-action:
Proof Proof of bn mtc action. Well-definedness of \rho_n is the coherence theorem for braided monoidal categories: the assignment \sigma_i \mapsto c_i satisfies the braid relations \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i = \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} by the hexagon axiom for c, and \sigma_i \sigma_j = \sigma_j \sigma_i for |i - j| \geq 2 by the interchange law.

Non-factorisation through S_n: the symmetric group relation \sigma_i^{\,2} = e would force \rho_n(\sigma_i^{\,2}) = c_{\mathbf{V}, \mathbf{V}}^{\,2} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{V} \otimes \mathbf{V}} on the i-th factor. But by the non-symmetric braiding clause of def:observable-mtc there exists a simple \mathbf{V} with c_{\mathbf{V},\mathbf{V}}^{\,2} \neq \mathrm{id}, which contradicts the symmetric-group relation. \square

Corollary. The tensor powers \mathbf{V}^{\otimes n} carry fractional statistics: particle exchange acts by a B_n-representation that distinguishes the braid \sigma_i from its inverse \sigma_i^{-1}, in contrast with the symmetric-group action seen by q = 1 observables (rem:u1-phase-tube).
sec:ns-approaches-intro: The classical Navier--Stokes regularity question sits inside a one-parameter family of q-deformed equations that are expected, but not yet proved, to be well-posed for q > 1. The degeneration at q = 1 forms a research programme. This section treats the classical limit as a phase transition and conjectures a critical exponent for the enstrophy divergence. The universality conjecture predicts that this exponent depends only on the Euler characteristic. It formulates a q-deformed Aubin--Lions compactness conjecture; because \nu_q \to 0, its limit object is an Euler solution. Conditional on these conjectures, the representation-theoretic truncation at roots of unity then locates the remaining gap in the growth rate of the core aspect ratio. Subsequent remarks track the geometry of vortex-line twist via the Levi scalar and compute core-shape evolution under Townsend strain dynamics. Finally, the section records the definition and known L^3 exclusions for discretely self-similar Leray profiles alongside their integer-spin spherical-harmonic truncations.
def:qns-unit-layers:
Definition Unit layers of the q-NS classical limit: aether (vanishing \nu_q) and physical (c_q-rescaled, \nu_{\mathrm{phys}} = 1/(2q)). The classical limit q \to 1^+ of the internal q-Navier–Stokes dynamics may be taken in two unit systems, which differ by the canonical aether scale c_q = 1/(q-1). Every statement about the classical limit of a q-fluid quantity carries exactly one of the two layer tags below.

Algebraic layer. Coordinates (x, t) as carried by the aether: wavenumbers are the q-integers [n]_q, and the viscosity is the derived ladder quantity

  \nu_q \;=\; \frac{q-1}{2q},

which vanishes as q \to 1^+. In this layer the classical limit is a vanishing-viscosity (Euler-type) limit.

Physical layer. Coordinates (X, T) = (c_q\,x,\; c_q\,t) with velocity unrescaled — a rescaling by an existing derived scale, introducing no new degree of freedom. Under this map k_{\mathrm{phys}} = (q-1)\,k_{\mathrm{sub}} (the ladder becomes a continuum grid of spacing q-1), enstrophies convert by (q-1)^2, and the viscosity becomes

  \nu_{\mathrm{phys}} \;=\; c_q\,\nu_q \;=\; \frac{1}{2q},

exactly — an algebraic identity, with \tfrac12 - \nu_{\mathrm{phys}} \leq (q-1)/2. In this layer the classical limit is a fixed-viscosity Navier--Stokes limit, matching the fixed-viscosity classical PDE regime.

Never straddle the layers (strict). A single computed quantity, estimate, or claim must not mix aether-layer and physical-layer inputs; every fluid-dynamics statement about the classical limit names its layer, and cross-layer comparisons go through the conversion identities above. The two layers can give different answers to the same-sounding question: the spectral pile-up question of the uniformity reduction is answered negatively in the algebraic layer (tail enstrophy above a fixed band grows without bound as q \to 1^+, the receding dissipation range filling in) and affirmatively in the physical layer (the converted tail vanishes), as measured numerically.
prop:qns-shell-tail-collapse:
Proposition Per-amplitude tail collapse in the discrete q-shell hierarchy. Let K be a linearly ordered field, \nu > 0 a viscosity, \delta \geq 0 a time step, and (k_n)_{n \geq 0} positive wavenumbers with \delta\,\nu k_n^2 \leq 1.

  1. (Per-rung equilibrium.) A rung u : \mathbb{N} \to K with u(0) = 0, forced by a constant F \geq 0 and damped at its own dissipation rate,

    u(t+1) \;\leq\; u(t) + \delta\bigl(k_n F - \nu k_n^2\, u(t)\bigr),

    satisfies u(t) \leq F/(\nu k_n) for every t.

  2. (Trajectory composition.) For a rung family u_n(t) \geq 0 with u_{n+1}(0) = 0, boundary bound \sup_t u_0(t) \leq P, and each rung forced by the square of the actual trajectory below it, every rung obeys the composed bound u_n(t) \leq B_n, where B_0 = P and B_{n+1} = B_n^2/(\nu k_{n+1}).

  3. (Geometric collapse.) If in addition the dissipation-scale condition B_n \leq \theta\,\nu k_{n+1} holds with 0 \leq \theta \leq 1, then

    u_n(t) \;\leq\; \theta^{\,n} P \qquad \text{for all } n, t.

  4. (Stability under nonlocal transfer.) The equilibrium and the collapse persist when each rung is forced by its two predecessors with weight \gamma \geq 0 (pairwise maxima decay at rate \theta per pair), and when every pair of rungs is coupled with geometric weight \lambda^{\,n-m-1}, 0 \leq \lambda < 1 (every rung beyond the band is uniformly \theta-suppressed under B \leq \theta(1-\lambda)\nu k_n).
rem:qns-shell-tail-collapse-interpretati:
Remark Scope and measured support for the q-shell tail collapse. In the physical layer of def:qns-unit-layers the hypotheses of prop:qns-shell-tail-collapse are \varepsilon-free: the viscosity satisfies \nu_{\mathrm{phys}} \geq 1/4 for 1 < q \leq 2, and the active block's physical wavenumbers k_{\mathrm{phys}} = q^n - 1 stay bounded on the aether window. The proposition therefore delivers a tail bound whose constants survive the classical limit q \to 1^{+}.

Numerical evolution of the DN q-shell system supports each hypothesis along actual trajectories. The dissipation-scale crossing exists at every tested \varepsilon, sits below the Kolmogorov estimate 2^{3/4}\varepsilon^{1/4} in physical wavenumber, and moves toward the infrared as \varepsilon \to 0. The per-rung equilibrium ratio stays below 1 on every excited rung — for nearest-neighbour transfer (maximum 0.90), second-neighbour transfer at equal strength, all-pairs geometric coupling at decay \lambda = 0.9, and the modulus dynamics of the complex Sabra system. Replacing the Sabra phases by decorrelated ones lowers every tail supremum by factors of 4 to 90, so the coherent evolution bounded by the proposition is the extremal case within this model class.

The statements are internal to the discrete shell hierarchy of a quantum observable universe. Spatial advection — the transport of structures through physical space by large scales — lies outside every shell model, real or complex, and marks the boundary of what this proposition constrains.
def:leray-profile:
Definition Discretely self-similar Leray profile. Within a QOU (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau). This block defines a class of classical velocity fields on \mathbb{R}^3. It asserts nothing about their existence.

Definition (discretely self-similar Leray profile). Fix a point x_0 \in \mathbb{R}^3 and a time T^*. Leray's similarity variables are

y = \frac{x - x_0}{\sqrt{T^* - t}}, \qquad s = -\log(T^* - t), \qquad t < T^* .

A Leray profile is a vector field V(y, s) on \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}, and the velocity field it defines is

v(x, t) = (T^* - t)^{-1/2}\, V\bigl(y, s\bigr).

The profile is discretely self-similar with period P > 0 if V(y, s + P) = V(y, s) for all y and s. It is steady if V does not depend on s.

Writing \lambda = e^{P/2} > 1, periodicity in s implies the discrete scaling invariance

v(x, t) = \lambda\, v\bigl(x_0 + \lambda (x - x_0),\; T^* - \lambda^2 (T^* - t)\bigr),

which for x_0 = 0, T^* = 0 is v(x, t) = \lambda\, v(\lambda x, \lambda^2 t). Conversely, invariance for all x and all t < T^* gives back periodicity in s by the inverse change of variables. A steady profile is discretely self-similar for every period.

The field v solves the Navier--Stokes equation with viscosity \nu if and only if V solves the Leray system

\partial_s V - \nu \Delta_y V + \tfrac{1}{2} V + \tfrac{1}{2} (y \cdot \nabla_y) V + (V \cdot \nabla_y) V + \nabla_y \Pi = 0, \qquad \nabla_y \cdot V = 0 ,

with pressure profile \Pi(y, s). The known constraints on nonzero solutions are collected in Exclusions for discretely self-similar profiles; finite truncations are discussed in Truncations of the Leray system.
rem:leray-profile-exclusions:
Remark Exclusions for discretely self-similar Leray profiles. The following results constrain a nonzero discretely self-similar Leray profile V solving the Leray system. Throughout, P = 2 \log \lambda is the period and \lambda > 1 the scaling factor.

Steady profiles. A steady profile V \in L^3(\mathbb{R}^3) solving the Leray system is zero [necas-ruzicka-sverak1996]. The same holds for V \in L^q, 3 < q \leq \infty, and for solutions satisfying local energy estimates [tsai1998].

Profiles in L^3. The L^3 norm is invariant under the Leray rescaling, so along the field v it equals \|V(\cdot, s)\|_{L^3} at s = -\log(T^* - t), a periodic function of s. If it is continuous in s it is bounded, so it does not tend to +\infty as t \to T^{*-}. Since \|v(t)\|_{L^3} \to \infty at any blow-up time [seregin2012], no discretely self-similar blow-up has a profile continuous in s with values in L^3; this is proved directly in [chae2013adss]. A bounded profile in L^2 lies in L^3, by \|V\|_{L^3}^3 \leq \|V\|_{L^\infty} \|V\|_{L^2}^2, so finite-energy bounded profiles are excluded too.

The surviving decay class. A profile with |V(y, s)| = O(|y|^{-a}) and a > 1 is in L^3 at infinity. If instead |V(y, s)| \gtrsim |y|^{-a} for large |y|, uniformly in s, with a < 1, then |v(x, t)| \gtrsim |x - x_0|^{-a} (T^* - t)^{(a-1)/2}, which is unbounded as t \to T^{*-} at every fixed x \neq x_0. What remains is |V(y, s)| \sim |y|^{-1}, the scale-invariant decay, with V(\cdot, s) \notin L^3.

The scaling factor. Discretely self-similar blow-up with \lambda close to 1 is excluded under a scale-critical bound, and such a blow-up has a single singular point [chae-wolf2016dss]. For \lambda well above 1 the question is open [bradshaw-tsai2018survey]. The period is not fixed by the QOU: the root-of-unity ladder q_\kappa = e^{i\pi/\kappa} satisfies q_\kappa^{2\kappa} = 1, and the aether parameter is not a root of unity.

Angular content. On the spin-j summand of an \mathrm{SU}(2)-representation the central element -1 acts by (-1)^{2j}. On velocity fields on \mathbb{R}^3 the rotation action factors through \mathrm{SO}(3), so -1 acts trivially and only integer j occur. The profile decomposes into vector spherical harmonics of integer degree.

Scope of finite models. The Descartes theorem is a statement about the global Euler class of the surface bundle, not a blow-up theorem for the Navier--Stokes equation on \mathbb{R}^3. A finite truncation of the Leray system is a Galerkin model. Finite-dimensional cascade models can blow up without the blow-up transferring to the unforced Navier--Stokes equation (Tao, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 29 (2016), 601--674), so a solution of a truncated system is evidence about the truncation only.
rem:leray-profile-construction:
Remark Truncations of the Leray system for a discretely self-similar profile. The Leray rescaling. In Leray's similarity variables y = (x - x_0)/\sqrt{T^* - t}, s = -\log(T^* - t), the velocity profile satisfies the Leray system. A continuous self-similar blowup would require a time-independent (s-independent) profile (V, \Pi) on \mathbb{R}^3; such a profile with V \in L^3(\mathbb{R}^3) is zero [necas-ruzicka-sverak1996], a no-go extended to L^q, 3 < q \leq \infty, and to local-energy estimates [tsai1998]. The profile considered here is therefore discretely self-similar: periodic in s with some period P > 0. The Leray system itself does not fix P.

The period. An identification of P with the scaling \lambda_\kappa of the root-of-unity ladder q_\kappa = e^{i\pi/\kappa} would require evaluating at a root of unity, which the aether parameter excludes. No identification of P is made here.

The angular decomposition. A velocity field on \mathbb{R}^3 decomposes in angle into vector spherical harmonics of integer degree \ell: the sphere is S^2 = \mathrm{SU}(2)/\mathrm{U}(1), and functions or vector fields on it carry only integer spin. Half-integer components j = 1/2, 3/2, \ldots do not occur in a Navier--Stokes velocity field. The quadratic term (V \cdot \nabla) V couples degrees \ell_1 and \ell_2 to every degree \ell with |\ell_1 - \ell_2| \le \ell \le \ell_1 + \ell_2, so a finite set of degrees is in general not closed under the nonlinearity.

Truncation. Consequently a truncation at finitely many degrees \ell \le L is a Galerkin approximation of the Leray system, not an exact reduction. A discretely self-similar profile depends on s periodically; after expansion in Fourier modes in s, the truncated system is a system of ODEs in the radial variable r indexed by both the angular degree and the Fourier mode. A truncation keeping only the zero Fourier mode is s-independent and is the steady case excluded above.

Boundary conditions. Each radial coefficient must be regular at r = 0, with the vanishing order set by its degree \ell and the type of vector spherical harmonic. At r \to \infty the profile must decay like r^{-1} and no faster. Decay faster than r^{-1} puts a bounded profile in L^3, and a discretely self-similar blow-up whose profile is continuous in s with values in L^3 is excluded [chae2013adss]; in particular a bounded square-integrable profile lies in L^3 and is excluded. Decay slower than r^{-1} makes the velocity field unbounded away from the blow-up point. See Exclusions for discretely self-similar profiles.

Open question. The coefficients of the truncated system are not specified here. Writing them down from the vector-spherical-harmonic coupling, and then deciding whether a nonzero s-periodic solution exists and persists as L grows, is the open content of this construction. Any numerical solution of a truncated system is evidence about the truncation, not about the Leray system.
conj:regularity-breakdown:
Conjecture Regularity breakdown at q = 1 and a discretely self-similar blow-up scenario. Within a QOU (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau). Part A below concerns the QOU's internal q-Navier--Stokes flow. Part B is a statement about the classical Navier--Stokes equation on \mathbb{R}^3. Identifying the internal flow with the classical equation is the separate open categorical-to-classical bridge and is not asserted here.

The global regularity theorem (q-NS well-posedness) holds for every q > 1. The conjecture concerns the endpoint q = 1.

Conjecture (regularity breakdown).

Part A (the q-family). Define the enstrophy order parameter

\Omega(q) = \sup_{t \geq 0} \sum_k [k]_q^2\, |\hat{v}_k(t)|^2 .

The initial amplitudes |\hat{v}_k(0)| are held fixed in the algebraic layer of the unit layers, independently of q. For each q > 1, \Omega(q) < \infty. Part A asserts that, for suitable such data, \Omega(q) \to +\infty as q \to 1^+, with \Omega(q) \sim (q - 1)^{-\alpha} for some critical exponent \alpha > 0.

Part B (classical model). There exists a nonzero backward discretely self-similar solution of the classical Navier--Stokes equation on \mathbb{R}^3 with fixed viscosity, in the sense of the discretely self-similar Leray profile: a smooth profile V(y, s), periodic in s = -\log(T^* - t) with some period P > 0, with |V(y, s)| = O(|y|^{-1}) as |y| \to \infty and V(\cdot, s) \notin L^3(\mathbb{R}^3). No value of P is asserted.

Consequences and constraints.

  1. Enstrophy blow-up is a consequence of Part B. The enstrophy of the field is (T^* - t)^{-1/2} E(s) with E(s) = \|\nabla_y V(\cdot, s)\|_{L^2}^2. A periodic E that is positive somewhere makes the enstrophy unbounded as t \to T^{*-}. Independently, at any blow-up time \|\nabla v(t)\|_{L^2}^2 \geq c\,(T^* - t)^{-1/2} [leray1934].
  2. The singular set is a point. A discretely self-similar blow-up has a single singular point (x_0, T^*) [chae-wolf2016dss]. The earlier claim of concentration on a vortex sheet of spatial Hausdorff dimension 2 is withdrawn; it is incompatible with this and with d_H = 1 in the counterexample conjecture below.
  3. The decay class is forced. A steady profile in L^3 is trivial [necas-ruzicka-sverak1996], extended to L^q, 3 < q \leq \infty, and to local energy estimates [tsai1998]. The L^3 norm is invariant under the Leray rescaling, so along a discretely self-similar solution it is periodic in s; if it is continuous it is bounded, while \|v(t)\|_{L^3} \to \infty at any blow-up time [seregin2012]. Hence no discretely self-similar blow-up has a profile continuous in s with values in L^3 [chae2013adss]. A bounded square-integrable profile lies in L^3, so it is excluded as well. Faster decay than |y|^{-1} puts the profile in L^3; slower decay makes v(\cdot, T^*) unbounded away from x_0. This leaves |V| \sim |y|^{-1}.
  4. The scaling factor. Write P = 2 \log \lambda with \lambda > 1. Scaling factors \lambda close to 1 are excluded under a scale-critical bound [chae-wolf2016dss]; the case of \lambda well above 1 is open [bradshaw-tsai2018survey]. The period is not tied to the root-of-unity ladder q_\kappa = e^{i\pi/\kappa}: q_\kappa^{2\kappa} = 1, and the aether parameter is not a root of unity.
  5. Integer angular degrees only. On the spin-j summand the central element -1 \in \mathrm{SU}(2) acts by (-1)^{2j}, and on velocity fields on \mathbb{R}^3 it acts trivially, since the action factors through \mathrm{SO}(3). So only integer j occur.

Heuristics for Part A. The following explain why Part A is expected; none is a proof ingredient.

Loss of UV regularisation. At q = 1 the q-Laplacian eigenvalues degenerate from exponential to polynomial growth, [k]_1 = k, so the spectral gap that controls the cubic term in the enstrophy equation closes.

Viscosity vanishes. The quantum viscosity is \nu_q = (q - 1)/(2q), and \nu_q \to 0 as q \to 1^+. The formal q \to 1 endpoint of the q-family is therefore the Euler equation, not the Navier--Stokes equation with fixed viscosity. This is why Part A does not by itself say anything about Part B.

Cascade becomes continuous. The discrete transfer rates of the q-turbulence spectrum merge into a continuous cascade at q = 1.

What \Omega(1) = +\infty does and does not mean. \Omega(q) is a supremum over all t \geq 0. A quantity can be unbounded on [0, \infty) while bounded on every [0, T], so divergence of \Omega is not finite-time blow-up. The analogy with a second-order phase transition, with q in the role of temperature and \Omega as order parameter, is a heuristic; it is not derived from the QOU axioms.

Relation to classical finite-energy regularity. Classical three-dimensional regularity asks whether smooth finite-energy data for the unforced Navier--Stokes equation with fixed viscosity can blow up in finite time. A discretely self-similar solution with |V| \sim |y|^{-1} has infinite global energy, so Part B bears on finite-energy blow-up only as a candidate local asymptotic profile near (x_0, T^*); local asymptotics of this kind with profile continuous in s with values in L^3 \cap C^2 are again excluded [chae2013adss]. Part B records a local profile scenario that survives the exclusions listed above and remains open. Part A concerns an internal q-family whose unrescaled q \to 1^+ endpoint is inviscid Euler, so it does not reduce fixed-viscosity classical Navier--Stokes regularity to the limit q \to 1^+.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs. Generic categorical identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.

conj:critical-exponent:
Conjecture Critical exponent of the enstrophy divergence at q = 1. The regularity breakdown conjecture predicts that maximum enstrophy diverges as \Omega_{\max}(q) \sim (q-1)^{-\alpha} for some \alpha > 0.

From the enstrophy evolution, \frac{d\Omega}{dt} \leq \Lambda_q\Omega, where \Lambda_q = \frac{(C_q')^2E_0}{\nu_q} - \nu_q.

Computation of \Lambda_q asymptotics. Set \varepsilon = q - 1 \to 0^+.

  • Viscosity: \nu_q = \varepsilon/(2(1+\varepsilon)) = \varepsilon/2 + O(\varepsilon^2).
  • Sobolev constant: C_q'^2 \approx \pi^2/6 + O(\varepsilon^2).
  • Growth rate: \Lambda_q \approx \pi^2 E_0/(3\varepsilon) + O(1). So \Lambda_q \sim (q-1)^{-1} as q \to 1^+. The Gronwall bound gives exponential growth, which is too crude.

Refined estimate via cascade depth. The q-turbulence spectrum gives the cascade depth N_{\mathrm{eff}} = \lfloor \log_q (\mathrm{Re}_q^{3/4})\rfloor. At q = 1 + \varepsilon:

  \mathrm{Re}_q = \frac{2}{\varepsilon},
  \qquad
  N_{\mathrm{eff}}
  \approx \frac{3}{4}\frac{\ln(2/\varepsilon)}{\varepsilon}.

The maximum enstrophy of the truncated system with N modes is bounded by the Kolmogorov enstrophy sum \Omega_{\max} \leq \sum_{k=1}^N k^2E(k). With E(k) \sim k^{-5/3}, the sum is bounded by N^{4/3}. Exponential damping ensures higher modes contribute negligibly. The effective enstrophy is dominated by the first N_{\mathrm{eff}} modes:

  \Omega_{\max}(\varepsilon)
  \lesssim
  N_{\mathrm{eff}}^{4/3}
   \sim 
  \left(\frac{\ln(1/\varepsilon)}{\varepsilon}\right)^{4/3}.

Result (closure-dependent — two heuristic values, neither rigorous). The exponent depends on which turbulence closure is imposed on the enstrophy budget:

  • Dissipation closure. Imposing \varepsilon = \nu_q\,\Omega (mean dissipation = viscosity \times enstrophy) with \varepsilon bounded away from 0 gives \Omega_{\max} \sim \varepsilon/\nu_q \sim (q-1)^{-1}, i.e. \alpha = 1. This is the exact algebraic consequence of the closure, and is the same leading order as the crude Gronwall rate \Lambda_q \sim (q-1)^{-1} above.
  • Kolmogorov-cascade closure. Imposing E(k) \sim k^{-5/3} truncated at N_{\mathrm{eff}} gives \Omega_{\max} \lesssim N_{\mathrm{eff}}^{4/3} \sim (q-1)^{-4/3}\bigl(\ln(q-1)^{-1}\bigr)^{4/3}, i.e. \alpha = 4/3 with a logarithmic correction.
  \Omega_{\max}(q) \sim (q-1)^{-\alpha},
  \qquad
  \alpha = 1 \ \text{(dissipation closure)}
  \quad\text{vs.}\quad
  \alpha = \tfrac{4}{3} \ \text{(Kolmogorov closure, up to logs)}.

Neither closure is rigorous; the true \alpha is fixed by the actual q-Navier--Stokes enstrophy spectrum (the turbulence-closure problem) and is open. The two values bracket it under their respective hypotheses.

rem:ns-surreal-bound:
Remark Surreal rate comparison in the q \to 1^+ limit: cascade ceiling versus viscous gap. Within the q-deformed model, the asymptotic competition between cascade growth and viscous damping as q \to 1^+ admits a formal rate comparison in the surreal extension.

Let \varepsilon \in \mathrm{Der}(A) be a positive infinitesimal parameterising q = 1 + \varepsilon. In the q > 1 regime, the gap scale \Delta_q \asymp \varepsilon^3 acts as an effective dissipation scale alongside the conjectured Kolmogorov-closure enstrophy ceiling of the critical-exponent conjecture.

The surreal rate comparison. Near \varepsilon = 0, two formal rates are compared:

  • Dissipation gap \Delta_q \asymp \varepsilon^3 (damping scale of the unrescaled q-model)
  • Conjectured enstrophy ceiling \mathcal{Z}_q \asymp \varepsilon^{-4/3} (under the Kolmogorov-cascade closure)

By surreal rate calculus, \mathcal{Z}_q \cdot \varepsilon^{4/3} \asymp 1, while \Delta_q \asymp \varepsilon^3 is a positive infinitesimal. The inequality

  \mathcal{Z}_q \;>\; \Delta_q

holds in the surreal ordering: the posited cascade ceiling sits at higher \omega-order than the vanishing dissipation scale.

Scope. As \varepsilon \to 0^+, the posited enstrophy ceiling outruns the unrescaled gap scale in \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon). Because the unrescaled viscosity \nu_q = \varepsilon/(2(1+\varepsilon)) tends to zero and the standard-part bridge from surreal q-flows to classical Leray--Hopf solutions is an open conjecture, this comparison records formal \varepsilon-scaling inside the q-deformed model rather than proving finite-time blowup of the fixed-viscosity classical Navier--Stokes equation.
conj:universality:
Conjecture Universality of the critical exponent: dependence on \chi(A) alone. Conditional on the critical-exponent conjecture, let \alpha denote the exponent governing a conjectured power-law divergence \Omega_{\max}(q) \sim (q-1)^{-\alpha} of the internal q-NS enstrophy supremum as q \to 1^+ (such as the Kolmogorov-closure value \alpha = 4/3). This conjecture asserts that \alpha depends only on:

  1. The Euler characteristic \chi(A) of the Frobenius--Hopf object.
  2. The spatial dimension d = 3.
  3. The rank of the gauge group.

It does not depend on the initial data v_0, the energy E_0, or the detailed geometry of the state bundle.
rem:p4-universality-argument:
Remark Brane-tower argument for the critical exponent's dependence on \chi(A) alone. Argument from the brane tower. Euler characteristic stability states that \chi(E_n) = \chi(A) across the brane tower. The critical exponent \alpha is determined by two quantities that depend only on this uniform structure:

  1. The Sobolev constant scaling. The Sobolev constant C_q depends on the eigenvalue growth rate [k]_q^2. This is determined by the representation theory of \mathrm{SU}_q(2) — a categorical invariant.
  2. The cascade depth scaling. The number of active modes depends on \mathrm{Re}_q, which is a function of q alone. The Kolmogorov scaling \Omega \sim N^{5/3} follows from d = 3 and quadratic nonlinearity.

The initial energy E_0 affects the prefactor of the enstrophy evolution bound, but not the exponent. The critical exponent \alpha = 4/3 derives from the cascade depth scaling.

Universality class. Different QOU realisations (different \chi(A)) could in principle give different \alpha, because \chi(A) affects the embeddable torus knot species, modifying the nonlinear interaction count.
rem:p4-universality-interpretation: Remark \alpha = 4/3 recast as an intrinsic topological invariant. Under the universality conjecture, a conjectured q \to 1^+ enstrophy-divergence exponent such as \alpha = 4/3 is framed as a universality-class invariant of the q-deformed model, determined by representation-theoretic data and surface topology rather than specific initial data in the algebraic unit layer.
conj:ns-counterexample:
Conjecture Conjectural anti-parallel vortex-collision singularity in the q \to 1^+ limit. Consider the q \to 1^+ degeneration of solutions to the q-NS model, proposing an anti-parallel vortex-pair scenario in which the limiting flow loses smoothness at a finite time T^*.

The initial data. Configure an anti-parallel vortex pair: two counter-rotating vortex tubes approaching each other by mutual induction. conj:q-aubin-lions:
Conjecture q-deformed Aubin--Lions lemma: compactness of the solution family as q \to 1.

Summary. A q-deformed Aubin–Lions compactness conjecture: the family \{v_q\}_{q>1} of q-NS solutions admits a subsequence converging strongly in L^2(0,T; \mathcal{H}) to a distributional solution of the Euler equation as q \to 1. Because the viscosity \nu_q tends to zero, the limit of the q-NS family itself is inviscid; a Navier--Stokes limit requires a modified family with a separate fixed viscosity (Step 6).

This would supply the compactness needed for the \{v_q\}_{q > 1} solutions to converge to a distributional solution of the Euler equation.

Step 1: Uniform embedding. Introduce the q-independent space \mathcal{H} = L^2(\mathcal{S}; T\mathcal{S}). For each q > 1, the fibre functor embeds L^2_q(A) \hookrightarrow \mathcal{H} with uniformly bounded embeddings. The fibre functor preserves inner products up to a factor controlled by the aether parameter.

Step 2: Uniform energy bound. The energy inequality gives \sup_{t \geq 0} \lVert v_q(t) \rVert_{L^2_q}^2 \leq 2\lVert v_0 \rVert_{\mathcal{H}}^2 for q close to 1. The bound is uniform in q.

Step 3: Uniform dissipation bound. The standard H^1 bound diverges as q \to 1. A uniform H^s bound for s < 1 follows by interpolation. For s = 1/2, it diverges. Truncation is necessary. The finite cascade depth means only N_{\mathrm{eff}}(q) modes are active. The truncated family lives in a finite-dimensional subspace. For any fixed N, the family is precompact.

Step 4: Diagonal extraction. Extract a diagonal subsequence q_n \to 1 such that for every fixed N, the truncated solution converges. The limit is constructed mode by mode.

Step 5: The limit is a distributional solution. Taking q = q_n \to 1 along the diagonal, the viscous term vanishes. The q-Laplacian becomes the classical Laplacian. In the limit, the sequence satisfies the truncated Euler equation. Taking N \to \infty, the limit satisfies the inviscid Euler equation distributionally. This is consistent with the quantum viscosity vanishing at q = 1.

Step 6: A modified family with fixed viscosity. The q-NS family itself does not converge to Navier--Stokes. To obtain a Navier--Stokes limit one must change the family, adding an independent classical viscosity \nu > 0 that does not vanish with q - 1. For that modified family the same compactness argument would give a weak Navier--Stokes solution with viscosity \nu; the modified family is a separate object, not the brane q-NS of this chapter.

Step 7: Conjectured loss of smoothness in the limit. Under the anti-parallel vortex-pair collision scenario of the vortex-collision conjecture, the filaments are posited to approach at rate d(t) \sim \sqrt{T^* - t} with diverging vorticity as t \to T^{*-}: for q > 1, quantum pressure opposes core overlap, whereas in the q \to 1^+ limit Q_q \to 0.

Under the hypotheses above, there exists a subsequence q_n \to 1 such that v_{q_n} \to v^* weakly in L^2. v^* is a weak solution of the Euler equation (of the Navier--Stokes equation with viscosity \nu for the modified family of Step 6), satisfies the energy inequality, and is smooth off a singular set of Hausdorff dimension \leq 1.

conj:vorticity-lower-bound:
Conjecture Vorticity lower bound for anti-parallel filament collision as q \to 1. Conditional on q-Aubin--Lions. Let v^* be the weak limit as q \to 1 of the q-NS solution for anti-parallel vortex pair initial data. Let \omega^* = \nabla \times v^* and let d(t) be the separation between the two filament cores. There exist constants c_1, c_2 > 0 such that for all t < T^*:

  c_1\sqrt{T^* - t} \leq d(t) \leq c_2\sqrt{T^* - t},
  \qquad
  \lVert \omega^*(t) \rVert_{L^\infty} \geq \frac{c_1}{T^* - t},
  \qquad
  \int_0^{T^*} \lVert \omega^*(t) \rVert_{L^\infty}\,dt = +\infty.

These give, respectively, (a) separation decay, (b) a vorticity lower bound, and (c) BKM divergence. In particular, the limit solution v^* loses regularity at T^*.
rem:vorticity-lower-bound-argument:

conj:root-of-unity-truncation:
Conjecture Representation-theoretic truncation at roots of unity and the q = 1 accumulation. Conditional on q-deformed Aubin--Lions lemma: compactness of the solution family as q \to 1, Conjectural anti-parallel vortex-collision singularity in the q \to 1^+ limit, Critical exponent of the enstrophy divergence at q = 1, Blowup mechanism as Yekutieli lifting obstruction in the brane tower, Vorticity lower bound for anti-parallel filament collision as q \to 1, and Regularity breakdown at q = 1 and a discretely self-similar blow-up scenario.

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a QOU with aether parameter q not a root of unity (QOU axiom). As q \to 1 through the roots of unity q = e^{i\pi/\kappa}, the representation category truncates to a finite modular tensor category; any singular behaviour in the model can arise only in the \kappa \to \infty accumulation. Within this conditional anti-parallel vortex-pair model with core aspect ratio \kappa(t):

  \boxed{
    \text{limiting collision singularity}
    \iff
    \kappa(t) = O(1).
  }

Heuristic argument.

The QOU axiom requires that q is not a root of unity. Passing q \to 1 along roots of unity q = e^{i\pi/\kappa} truncates the representation theory to finitely many simple objects at each finite level \kappa, so any loss of smoothness in the family is confined to the infinite-level limit \kappa \to \infty.

The truncation mechanism — driven by the vanishing of the q-integer [\kappa]_q at q = e^{i\pi/\kappa}, which restricts the q-Laplacian spectral tower [k]_q^2 to the finite Verlinde/ADE set — is established in the q-Laplacian spectral tower. The paragraphs below trace its heuristic reading for the q-deformed fluid model.

Three regimes of \mathrm{SU}_q(2) representations.

  1. Generic q > 1 (QOU regime). Contains infinitely many simple objects V_j, j = 0, 1/2, 1, \ldots, with quantum dimensions [2j+1]_q > 0 and eigenvalues [k]_q^2 \sim q^{2k} growing exponentially. Conditional global regularity models smooth evolution in this regime.
  2. Root of unity q = e^{i\pi/\kappa}, bounded \kappa \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 2}. Contains finitely many simple objects, j = 0, 1/2, \ldots, (\kappa-2)/2, since [2j+1]_q = 0 at j = (\kappa-1)/2. The Verlinde formula governs fusion:
    N_{ij}^k
    = \int_0^1 \frac{S_{ik}S_{jk}}{S_{0k}}dk,

where S is the modular S-matrix, yielding a modular tensor category at level \kappa. 3. q = 1 (classical limit). Contains infinitely many simple objects with [k]_1 = k (polynomial scaling); both the root-of-unity truncation and the exponential q > 1 damping disappear.

Finite-dimensionality at each root of unity.

At a fixed root of unity q = e^{i\pi/\kappa}, a truncated q-NS Galerkin model retains at most (\kappa-1)/2 active vortex modes:

  • Within generic q > 1: modes above [k]_q > \mathrm{Re}_q^{1/2} undergo exponential damping while remaining nonzero.
  • At a root of unity: modes with j > (\kappa-2)/2 vanish in the quotient category, leaving a finite-dimensional ODE system that is globally smooth by Picard--Lindelöf.

The q = 1 accumulation.

As \kappa \to \infty, q = e^{i\pi/\kappa} \to 1 and the cutoff j_{\max} = (\kappa-2)/2 \to \infty unlocks infinitely many modes. Under the conditional hypotheses above, no fixed finite truncation blows up, so any singularity of the limiting family is purely an infinite-mode accumulation effect as \kappa \to \infty.

Connection to the core aspect ratio.

At a fixed root of unity q = e^{i\pi/\kappa}, restricting core-boundary Fourier modes to j \leq (\kappa-2)/2 models the core aspect ratio \kappa(t) = a_\perp/a_\parallel by a trigonometric polynomial of degree at most (\kappa-1)/2, obeying the Bernstein inequality |\kappa'(t)| \leq N\|\kappa\|_\infty. Within this finite-mode ansatz, one obtains a level-dependent upper bound

  \sup_{t < T^*} \kappa(t)
   \leq 
  1 + C \cdot (\kappa - 1)

for a constant C independent of \kappa, which diverges linearly as \kappa \to \infty (q \to 1).

The conditional growth-rate question.

The conditional vorticity lower bound requires uniform control \sup_t \kappa(t) \leq C independent of \kappa, whereas the finite-mode bound 1 + C(\kappa-1) grows with \kappa. Within this collision ansatz, three asymptotic regimes are distinguished:

  • If \kappa(t) \leq C_0 uniformly in \kappa: the core cross-section remains of bounded aspect ratio and the conditional lower bound of the vorticity lower bound yields singular vorticity growth as t \to T^{*-}.
  • If \kappa(t) \sim \kappa: the core flattens into a sheet at the rate new modes unlock, so the lower bound \omega \geq c/(T^*-t) need not hold and the limiting flow may remain regular.
  • If \kappa(t) \sim \kappa^\beta with 0 < \beta < 1: the ansatz predicts singular concentration only for \beta < 1/2.

Geometric scope of \kappa(t). The core aspect ratio \kappa(t) measures the cross-sectional core shape only and cannot be identified with a Levi-form condition number \lambda_{\max}/\lambda_{\min}. On the three-dimensional flow domain the Levi datum of the vorticity plane field is the single scalar \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi (core Levi form), so there is no eigenvalue pair and no condition number, and any direct blow-up implication from non-degenerate Levi data is refuted by steady Beltrami solutions (Levi degeneracy conjecture).

A state sum written with them has infinitely many labels, and its convergence is not established. The constructions themselves apply to the truncated categories at q = e^{i\pi/\kappa}; how their \kappa \to \infty behaviour relates to q_0 is a separate analytic question that this remark does not address.

The invariance of these state sums under a flip of a surface triangulation is an associativity (F-move) identity. rem:townsend-biot-savart-strain:
Remark Townsend evolution under Biot--Savart strain: the first-order core flattening \kappa \to 0. This computes the asymptotic behaviour of the core aspect ratio at the vortex-collision time T^\ast. First, the singular Biot–Savart strain is used, valid when cores are well separated. Next, the hyperbolic saturation is used that takes over when cores overlap.

Setup. Two anti-parallel vortex filaments with circulation \Gamma approach head-on at collision time T^\ast. The cross-section of each viscous core is modelled by the Townsend covariance matrix: V_1(t) is the squared core radius in the stretching direction, and V_2(t) is the squared core radius in the compression direction. The external strain rate induced by one filament on the other is \alpha(t) = 1/(2(T^\ast - t)). The leading behaviour is convention-independent. The strain rate is independent of \Gamma.

Townsend evolution. Under axisymmetric viscous strain, the squared core radii satisfy

  \frac{dV_1}{dt} = +2\,\alpha(t)\,V_1 + 2\nu,
  \qquad
  \frac{dV_2}{dt} = -2\,\alpha(t)\,V_2 + 2\nu.

Substituting \alpha(t) = 1/(2\tau) for the time remaining \tau = T^\ast - t gives a linear system.

Exact solutions. As the collision is approached (\tau \to 0), the stretching coordinate diverges (V_1(\tau) \sim C_1/\tau \to \infty) and the compressing coordinate vanishes (V_2(\tau) \sim -2\nu\,\tau \ln\tau \to 0).

The first-order shape prediction. The squared core aspect ratio is \kappa^2(\tau) = V_2(\tau)/V_1(\tau) \to 0. Viscous diffusion flattens the core into a two-dimensional sheet. This is a statement about the shape of the core cross-section, under the point-vortex assumption. It carries no Levi information. With the plane field \ker\varTheta = \xi^\perp of The Levi datum of the vorticity plane field is the single scalar \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi, a straight anti-parallel pair has \xi = \pm e_z on each core, so its Levi scalar \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi is 0 whatever the core shape. Flattening therefore neither creates nor removes a Levi degeneration. The straight pair satisfies the hypothesis of branch (B) of Levi degeneracy conjecture for every core shape, and it is regular for a different reason: its vorticity is \omega_z(x, y)\,e_z, so the flow is two-dimensional.

Breakdown of the approximation. The Biot–Savart strain rate assumes a point-vortex geometry. But V_1(\tau) \to \infty while d(\tau)^2 \to 0. The two cross over at a finite \tau_\ast, after which the filaments overlap. The Biot–Savart kernel is no longer valid. The strain field near the collision plane is the merged flow of a single interaction zone. The apparent flattening \kappa \to 0 is an artefact of the failed approximation.
rem:hyperbolic-overlap-saturation:
Remark Hyperbolic-overlap strain saturation: the core aspect ratio locks at \kappa^2 = \pi\nu/(2\Gamma+\pi\nu). Once the stretching coordinate V_1 reaches the squared separation d^2, the point-vortex kernel breaks down. The local stream function shifts to a hyperbolic stagnation-point flow. The apparent flattening \kappa \to 0 reverses. Their merged interaction is an elliptic-section vortex sitting at a hyperbolic stagnation point. The strain rate is bounded by the overlapping cores themselves. The length scale is \sqrt{V_1}. The kernel rotates to a Burgers-like strain \alpha_{\mathrm{hyp}}(t) = \Gamma/(\pi V_1(t)).

Saturated Townsend system. Substituting \alpha_{\mathrm{hyp}} into the stretching equation gives a constant right-hand side. V_1 grows linearly with time and remains finite through to the formal collision time T^\ast. The exponential runaway is replaced by controlled linear growth. The strain saturates because the same coordinate driving the stretching also sets the length scale.

The V_2 relaxation rate is comparable to the V_1 growth rate, preventing quasi-steady equilibrium. Take the proportionality ansatz V_2(t) = \lambda V_1(t). The ODE forces

  \kappa^2

  \frac{V_2}{V_1}
  \;=\;
  \frac{\pi\nu}{2\Gamma + \pi\nu}.
  \;\;}

  2. The asymptotic value is the attracting proportionality ratio, not the naive Burgers equilibrium.
  3. The Townsend equations assume axisymmetric straining. Three-dimensional instabilities may modify the picture.

rem:crow-approach-amplification:
Remark Crow amplification during the pair approach is a bounded power law (d_0^2/V_{1,0})^{s^*/3}. The two-regime collision model of the Biot–Savart approach and the hyperbolic-overlap saturation treats the anti-parallel pair as two-dimensional. The named three-dimensional effect outside the model is the Crow instability: sinusoidal displacement perturbations of an anti-parallel filament pair grow by mutual induction at rate

  \sigma \approx s^* \, \frac{\Gamma}{2\pi d^2},

with s^* \approx 0.8 at the classical optimal wavelength for core-to-separation ratio \approx 0.1.

Along the phase-1 approach d^2(t) = d_0^2 - (\Gamma/\pi)\,t, the accumulated perturbation growth to the overlap engagement d^2_{\mathrm{ov}} integrates in closed form:

  N_e \;=\; \int_0^{t_{\mathrm{ov}}} \sigma \, dt
      \;=\; \frac{s^*}{2}\,\ln\!\frac{d_0^2}{d^2_{\mathrm{ov}}},

and with the circulation-independent strain-race engagement d^2_{\mathrm{ov}} = d_0^2\,(V_{1,0}/d_0^2)^{2/3} the total linear amplification is the power law

  A \;=\; e^{N_e} \;=\; \left(\frac{d_0^2}{V_{1,0}}\right)^{s^*/3}
  \;\approx\; \left(\frac{d_0^2}{V_{1,0}}\right)^{0.27}.

These formulas bear on the two-dimensional reduction of the collision model. The e-fold count is logarithmic in the core ratio, so within linear theory there is no finite-time three-dimensional runaway during the approach: the perturbation amplification is bounded for every finite core. Viscosity tightens the bound further. When the viscous core-growth engagement precedes the strain-race engagement, the amplification is capped at the viscous crossing (numerically A \approx 6 at s^* = 0.8, \nu = 10^{-3}, independent of the core ratio below 10^{-4}). The bounded linear amplification does not settle the fate of perturbations that enter the overlap regime at finite amplitude: the nonlinear stage of the Crow instability drives vortex reconnection, a topology-changing process outside the two-regime model entirely. The three-dimensional escape from the model's regularisation picture therefore requires either large seed perturbations or the nonlinear regime; the linear stage alone degrades the two-dimensional reduction only polynomially in the core ratio.

Relation to the Levi degeneracy conjecture. The Crow mode is a bending of the filaments, and bending is the direction geometry that Levi degeneracy conjecture now concerns. That block records the standard necessary condition for blow-up: the vorticity line field must lose \tfrac{1}{2}-Hölder control on the high-vorticity set. A straight pair cannot meet it. The bounded linear amplification above gives bounded bending of a finite seed at the engagement separation, so the linear Crow stage does not produce that loss of control. Whether the nonlinear stage does is left open above. This is a statement about Crow linear theory alone, not an exclusion of the three-dimensional route.
rem:q-ns-research-programme:
Remark Open problems in the q-deformed Navier--Stokes programme. The conditional global regularity statement and the regularity-breakdown conjecture organise the brane q-Navier--Stokes model around a one-parameter family of deformed hydrodynamic equations and its q \to 1^+ degeneration.

Scope of the q-deformed formulation. For aether parameter q > 1, exponential growth of the q-Laplacian eigenvalues [k]_q^2 and positive induced viscosity \nu_q = (q - 1)/(2q) supply regularising mechanisms absent at q = 1. Studying q \to 1^+ probes how those internal mechanisms degenerate, while separating the unrescaled inviscid Euler limit (\nu_q \to 0) from fixed-viscosity classical Navier--Stokes dynamics on \mathbb{R}^3.

Five open problems in the q-NS programme.

Problem 1. Concrete q-NS evolution and unconditional well-posedness for q > 1. Construct a concrete q-NS evolution on \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}_2) and discharge the existence, uniqueness, and smoothness hypotheses of global regularity from the compact-resolvent and exponential-eigenvalue bounds of the q-Laplacian.

Problem 2. Enstrophy behaviour as q \to 1^+. Determine whether the algebraic-layer enstrophy supremum \Omega(q) diverges as q \to 1^+ (Part A of regularity breakdown) and, if so, determine the critical exponent \alpha in \Omega(q) \sim (q - 1)^{-\alpha} beyond heuristic closures.

Problem 3. Singular-set and vortex-line geometry. Clarify admissible singular-set and vortex-line twist configurations in the q \to 1^+ limit, testing branch (B) of the Levi degeneracy conjecture on the twist scalar \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi and separating point singularities of discretely self-similar profiles from filament-reconnection events (vortex reconnection, Berry moduli).

Problem 4. Universality across QOU realisations. Test whether any q \to 1^+ critical exponent depends only on the categorical invariants of the QOU (such as \chi(A) and gauge rank) or varies with initial data and modal coupling structure.

Problem 5. Compactness and unit-layer bridge at q \to 1^+. Establish compactness for q-NS trajectories as q \to 1^+ (toward weak Euler solutions in the unrescaled algebraic layer, or toward weak Navier--Stokes solutions in a c_q-rescaled or fixed-viscosity family) and determine whether acoustic horizon formation or vortex-pair approach produces genuine finite-time singularities.

Summary. Within the QOU model, the unconditionally proved fluid-dynamical results are algebraic — the Hecke two-vortex channel algebra, the \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}_2) q-Legendre triad bounds, discrete shell tail collapse, exact Beltrami flows, and global surface Euler classes — while unconditional q > 1 well-posedness and classical three-dimensional regularity or blowup at q = 1 are open questions.
